name: MVTec AD
ability_definition: The ability to tell when something is wrong or is likely to go wrong. It does not involve solving the problem, only recognizing that there is a problem.

task_realism.reasoning: The task is real: spotting scratches, cracks, contamination, and missing parts on manufactured goods is genuine quality-control work that exercises problem sensitivity. The defects are real, not synthetic. But it is only one workplace instance of the ability. The objects are cleanly staged, and the defect types are fairly visible compared with the subtle, ambiguous signs workers must often notice.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Images are taken under controlled lighting and alignment with fixed camera setups. The test sets have a far higher defect rate than real production lines, where anomalies are rare. Image-level AUROC is threshold-free, so it hides the operating-point trade-off between false alarms and misses that real inspectors must make. There is no time pressure, no cost of error, no drift in the input distribution over time, and no multi-view or contextual information.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only static, single-image visual anomaly detection in industrial objects and textures. It leaves out the forward-looking part of the ability ('likely to go wrong'). It also leaves out non-visual and multimodal cues such as sounds, trends, and behavior, and other domains such as medical, safety, social, financial, and software. It does not test whether a model can detect problems that were never defined as deviations from a clean training distribution.

format_match.reasoning: The inputs are high-resolution photographs of real products, which resemble automated optical inspection data. The outputs are anomaly scores and pixel maps, which are plausible artifacts for an inspection system. However, the images are pre-cropped and centered on a single object, and there is no escalation or reporting output of the kind a human would produce.

transferability_reasoning: MVTec AD is a realistic, well-constructed test of one concrete form of problem sensitivity: noticing visual defects in manufactured items after learning only what normal looks like. Its controlled imaging, inflated defect rate, and threshold-free metric depart from real inspection conditions. Its restriction to static visual industrial inspection covers only a narrow slice of a broad, cross-domain, partly anticipatory ability, which limits how far high scores transfer to general workplace problem sensitivity.

2020.metric: image-level AUROC (%), averaged over all 15 MVTec AD classes
2020.human_reference: Specialist workforce: industrial visual quality-control inspectors, i.e. people whose job is to spot defective parts and surfaces.

2021.metric: image-level anomaly detection AUROC (%), mean over 15 MVTec AD categories
2021.human_reference: Specialist workforce: industrial visual quality inspectors (median trained inspector), who judge whether a part or texture image shows a defect after seeing examples of normal parts.
